Subject: APAC hosting evidence request — KMS & private-link separation

Jordan — thanks for the demo earlier. RetailCo has two requests we need documented before we move the pilot into procurement: 1) Strong evidence that APAC-hosted instances (Tokyo region) do not share KMS keys or key material with US/EU tenants (we need explanation + an artifact showing key partitioning), and 2) a simple diagram and control description for the private-link/VPC endpoints used for private deployments (we need assurance the control plane does not egress through non-APAC regions).

Can you send the artifacts or point us to where we can download signed evidence? Our security team expects something they can attach into the SIG/CAIQ response. If possible, include the operational owner we can call for a short technical walkthrough.

Appreciate it — Samir
RetailCo, Director of Cloud Security

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>

Samir, Jordan — adding technical details below (summary + quick evidence pointers). Full diagram attached (redwood-apac-kms-segmentation-diagram.pdf) and a VPC flow PNG (apac-vpc-endpoint-flow.png).

Summary (technical):
- Physical hosting: Redwood's Tokyo region runs in a single cloud region per customer deployment when Private/VPC is selected; control plane endpoints for Redwood Private are deployed into the customer VPC via a customer-managed private link when requested (no default public egress from compute).

- KMS model: we support two modes for APAC private deployments:
  1) Customer-managed KMS (recommended): Customer provisions a KMS key in their Tokyo account. We integrate via a customer KMS alias; all tenant encryption for that deployment is bound to the customer key, and we never export key material. Evidence: see attachment snippet (redwood-soc2-snapshot-2026Q1.txt) showing KMS integration workflow and the KMS alias naming convention (apac-cust-<tenant-id>-kms).
  2) Redwood-managed regional keys: for hosted or self-service where customers decline CMK, we provision a regional key isolated to Tokyo and scoped per-tenant. Keys are tagged with region=ap-northeast-1 and tenant-id; cryptographic material is never shared across regions or tenants.

- Audit & controls: Cloud audit logs (KMS API calls), key policy examples, and an HSM-backed provider are used; logs are retained per our standard retention (90 days by default, extended windows by contract). The SOC2 snapshot attachment includes a sample KMS request log and operator audit record (redacted).

- Private-link / VPC flow: When Private is enabled we create VPC endpoints and route tables that bind compute to the customer's subnets. Control plane components can be deployed either in the customer's VPC (private control plane) or in an isolated customer-dedicated subnet in Redwood-managed account but accessed only over the private link; we will provide a signed network diagram depending on the deployment mode you choose.

Next steps (proposed):
- Jordan: share the attached diagrams to RetailCo security (done)
- Samir: confirm whether you prefer customer-managed KMS (CMK) in your Tokyo account or Redwood-managed tenant keys
- If CMK chosen: provide KMS ARN and an operator contact to authorize the cross-account grant

Thanks — Marcus
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Samir — quick follow-up after Marcus' notes. Per your procurement checklist we have: 

1) Attached diagram PDFs and the SOC2 snapshot (attached). The diagrams are signed and stamped by our infra team lead; you can attach them to the SIG/CAIQ response.
2) If you select CMK: we will require a cross-account grant with the KMS ARN. We provided the KMS alias pattern in Marcus' note (apac-cust-<tenant-id>-kms).
3) Control plane egress: for a Private deployment with the private control plane option, no control-plane traffic exits the APAC region. If you take the Redwood-managed control plane option, control plane endpoints remain in the same APAC availability zones and do not route through US/EU. We will include that statement as a signed appendix if needed.

I'll schedule a 30-min technical walkthrough for Tue 31 Mar at 09:00 JST — let me know if that works or propose another time.
